script.stored_text_completeness: All 18818 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 2 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("worrying enough for both of you."); list is numbered 1, 3-13 with sign 2 unlabelled and a "7 and 1/2"; ASR garbles ("Their feet" for feed, "the the 7 grand", "outperforming" likely "overspending"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Drive down any suburban cul-de-sac in America right now and count the trucks. Not just any trucks, the loaded ones. Lifted F-150s, Stormtrooper white Tahoes, a matching his and hers Range Rover situation that costs more than a starter home. Manicured lawns, paver driveways, a boat peaking out of the third garage bay, and you think, "Man, everyone on this street is doing great." They're not. A lot of them are one missed bonus away from a hardship withdrawal and
script.ending_words: the family Christmas photo in front of a professionally decorated tree, he just took a $6,000 hardship withdrawal to cover December. He posted about a ski trip that same week. Wealth is what you don't see, debt is what you do, and the loudest driveway on the block almost always belongs to the person you should be worrying about the least because they're already worrying enough for both of you.
script.analysis: Full 18818 canonical characters read. A numbered list essay: cul-de-sac hook; car-payment and paycheck-to-paycheck stats; signs: multi-truck driveway, rolling negative equity, cheapest house on the fanciest street, empty McMansion, HELOC renovations, delivery habit, travel sports, private school, subscriptions, BNPL groceries, garage full of stuff, toy fleet, highlight reel and money dysmorphia, loudness about money; reframe on behaviour over income; stealth-wealth close (Ramsey millionaire study). Reproduces: boat payment, subscription annualisation, delivery spend, tuition gross-up. Wrong: two-truck payment understated (~$2,250 at 7%, not $1,900); $85/day boat cost wrong (~$1,065 per day used); "three-to-one" subscription gap is 2.5x; Stanley 30%-in-$300K-homes not located. Many statistics unchecked. The stored ending is complete.
